passage:
Every morning in the small hill town of Champhai, Damini stood at the school gate with her bag and her stomach clenched. The class chat had a post about her, and it felt as if the whole school had seen it. Twice that week she told her family she felt unwell.
On Thursday her friend Lalremsiami walked her home. "Is it the chat?" Damini nodded, eyes wet. "I think school scares me," she whispered, "and it feels silly."
"It isn't silly. Your fear is telling you something is wrong."
That night Damini showed her mother the phone. The next day they met the headmistress, who promised to look into the post and speak to the class. Damini walked in with her shoulders a little lower.

qa.q: When did Lalremsiami walk Damini home?
qa.a: Lalremsiami walked her home on Thursday.

qa.q: Why did Damini stand at the school gate with her stomach clenched?
qa.a: She dreads school because of the post about her in the class chat, and feels as if the whole school has seen it.

qa.q: What helped Damini deal with her fear?
qa.a: She told her friend and then her mother, and together they asked the headmistress to act, treating the fear as a signal rather than a weakness.

qa.q: How might the headmistress see the situation?
qa.a: The headmistress hears a student who is afraid to come to school because of a post, and sees it as the school's job to act, which is why she promised to look into it and speak to the class.

grounding: Shows a teen dreading school because of what is online, treating fear as a signal and asking adults and the school to act.

passage:
Sunday, 10 pm

I don't want to go to school tomorrow. I keep saying I have a stomach ache, but it's not that.

Someone posted a rumour about me in the Class 11 page on Friday, that I cheated my way into the science olympiad team. Now there are comments under it. Some people I don't even know. When I think of walking past the lockers, my heart starts racing and my hands go cold.

I thought feeling this scared meant I was weak. Vandana said it's the opposite. She messaged, "Your body is telling you something's wrong. Tell someone."

So tonight I told Mummy. I showed her the post and the comments. She sat with me on the bed and read every one. She said, "You're not weak for being scared. This is serious." She wrote to the counsellor and my class teacher right then, asking them to take the post down and speak to the class. She's coming with me to the counsellor at 8.

I still feel scared. But I'm not scared alone.

Seema

qa.q: What rumour was posted about Seema?
qa.a: The rumour said Seema cheated to get into the science olympiad team.

qa.q: What was Seema feeling when thinking about walking past the lockers?
qa.a: Seema felt frightened, with a racing heart and cold hands.

qa.q: What did Mummy do that helped?
qa.a: Mummy read every comment, told Seema being scared was not weakness, and wrote to the counsellor and class teacher that night asking them to act.

qa.q: How does Vandana see Seema's fear?
qa.a: Vandana sees it as a signal that something is wrong, not a weakness, and urges Seema to tell someone.

grounding: It shows a teen who dreads going to school because of an online rumour, learning that fear is a signal, and telling a parent who asks the school to act.

passage:
Sharmila: trisha i'm not coming tmrw
Trisha: again?? what's going on
Sharmila: the video. someone posted me tripping in PT with that stupid music. it's everywhere
Sharmila: i can't face them. i feel sick every morning
Trisha: that's not weakness. that's ur body saying something's wrong
Sharmila: or i'm just a coward
Trisha: no. u're scared because they're being cruel. that's normal
Trisha: have u told ur mom?
Sharmila: no. she'll make it a big thing
Trisha: it IS a big thing. u've missed 2 days
Trisha: tell her now and ask her to talk to the counsellor. schools have to act on this
Sharmila: ok. i'll show her

Sharmila walked into the kitchen with her phone. Her mother watched the video, then turned off the stove and hugged her. "I'm so sorry. You should never have had to hide this." She called the counsellor's number from the school diary that night and left a message asking for a meeting and for the video to be taken down.

qa.q: How many days had Sharmila missed?
What was Sharmila feeling about going to school?
qa.a: Sharmila felt sick every morning with dread and ashamed, even calling herself a coward.

qa.q: What did Trisha advise, and why was it wise?
qa.a: Trisha told Sharmila her fear was normal and urged her to tell her mother and ask the counsellor to act, because schools must respond to bullying.
She turned off the stove, hugged her, said she should never have had to hide it, and called the counsellor that night.

grounding: It shows a teen dreading school because of a mocking video online, learning fear is a signal and not weakness, and telling a parent who asks the school to act.
